title: Fix ScheduleSpec.weekly/.rolling to throw ArgumentError instead of assert() (silently unenforced in release builds)

evidence.quote: Throws [ArgumentError] when [daysOfWeek] is empty or contains values

why: WeeklySchedule and RollingSchedule enforce their invariants with Dart `assert()`, which the compiler strips out of release builds entirely (only active in debug/profile). Both factory doc comments explicitly promise 'Throws ArgumentError' — that promise is false in the exact build users run. `fromParts` (same file, line 63) feeds `daysOfWeek ?? const []` directly into `WeeklySchedule(...)` whenever the DB/JSON column is null, and the independent JSON codec path in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:346-349 does the same for a missing `days_of_week`/`days` key, wrapped in a try/catch that only rescues the debug-mode AssertionError — in release it silently produces a `WeeklySchedule([])`. A stage with an empty day-list never matches any weekday, so its chazara review permanently stops being scheduled with no error, no log, and no user-facing signal.
recommendation: Replace both asserts with explicit `if (...) throw ArgumentError(...)` (matching the pattern already used correctly by ScopeLevel/StageOrder/Pin/DayKind/CalendarSystem in the same directory) so the invariant holds in release builds too.
acceptance_criteria: ScheduleSpec.weekly([]) and ScheduleSpec.rolling(0)/.rolling(-1) throw ArgumentError when run under `flutter test` compiled in release/profile mode (or any assert-disabled run), not just debug.

New test/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec_test.dart exists and is wired into the test suite, covering empty/out-of-range daysOfWeek, non-positive windowSize, and fromParts with a null daysOfWeek column.
AG-5 mirroring restored: lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart has a corresponding test file (currently missing).

corrections: Rule citation 'EH-4' is a loose fit — EH-4's actual text concerns typed catch clauses / throwing only Exception-Error subclasses, not assert()-vs-ArgumentError release-mode stripping. The more relevant standard is the docstring's own documented contract plus AG-5 (missing test mirror), both correctly cited. Does not change the verdict since the defect and its evidence are independently confirmed.

The "why" narrative's claim that this bug causes chazara scheduling to silently stop is not supported — scheduler_engine.dart's actual scheduling decision reads `daysOfWeek` from raw JSON via SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl, never through ScheduleSpec/WeeklySchedule, so the assert-vs-throw defect cannot produce that consequence. Real impact is confined to `StageDefinition`/`.schedule` consumers (edit/export screens) via `_rowToModel`/`fromParts`, where release mode yields `WeeklySchedule([])` while debug mode's `catch (_)` swallows the AssertionError into `DelaySchedule(0)` — a data-model inconsistency, not a scheduling outage. The cited rule EH-4 (typed catch clauses / never catch Error subtypes) does not match this defect class; the actual violation is an undocumented (in coding-standards.md, "assert" appears nowhere) assert-vs-explicit-validation contract break.
